label: paragraph_title
text: TYPHOON TOLL AT COAST PORT.

label: text
text: Yeung Kong Fleet Tragedy.

label: text
text: GALLANT RESCUE BY BRITISH STEAMER "HYDRANGEA."

label: text
text: Three thousand lives are believed to have perished in the typhoon, the victims being of the Yeung Kong fishing fleet.

label: text
text: The thrilling experiences of the crews of fishing fleets from Yeung Kong in Chinese territory (not far from Macao) were related by the survivors of ten junks who were rescued from the wreckage by Captain R. Elvidge of the s.s. "Hydrangea" between 2 and 6.15 p.m. yesterday, south of Hong Kong, the exact position being given at Lat. 21.7 No. Long. 111.10 E.

label: text
text: Captain Elvidge in his report stated that the ten junks were a mass of wreckage, four of them considered to be dangerous to navigation within a radius of five miles of the position given.

label: text
text:
Rescue Under Difficulties
Heavy-sens were running at the time and the rescue of 35 survivors who were clinging for dear life to the wreckage was effected with considerable difficulty—a fent accomplished with great gallantry and at the risk of the lives of the crew of the vessel. Wreckage was floating about all around.

label: text
text: Passengers on the vessel were moved to sympathy at the pitiful appearance of the survivors as one by one they were Huiled on to the deck clad in what little rags were left after the fury of the storm.

label: text
text: A voluntary subscription among the crew and passengers of the "Hydrangea" realised the sum of $200 which was handed to the survivors to help them in their sad "ghts". The recipients gratefully knowledged the gift.

label: text
text: When they were sufficiently recovered from their long immersion in the water and fluttering by the waves, with the careful attention given by the crew and passengers on board, the survivors related their experiences from the time they were caught by the typhoon until they were rescued.

label: text
text: It appears from their narrative that the 35 men were part of the crews of ten junks which were out at sea on Monday morning.

label: text
text: At that time there were about 130 other junk within sight of each other all carrying out their occupation with nothing to indicate the fate which was in store for them.

label: text
text: The typhoon struck the junk's at 10 o'clock in the morning and almost without exception as far as those who lived to tell the tale could see, all the junk's capsized in the terrific gale which kept on continuously for about 14 hours.

label: text
text: Those rescued formed only a small part of the crews of the ten junks which were carried away by wind and wave, as one by one dropped out exhausted. They had been allout for 36 hours.
